reasoning: Set A has the stronger RL design and covers the ground truth more fully. It has random and scripted baselines in every environment, a tabular→DQN ladder with reward shaping, a REINFORCE→PPO ladder, a co-learning ladder with controls for each side, and a tournament. But its build layer is stale against its own design. The architecture added sides and schedules late (AD-16, AD-17, 'M1 is at 0 of 20 tasks… must be rechecked before the build starts'), and the M1 plan was never replanned. M1-T03 builds the retired `registry.make_agent`, and the context packets for M1-T01 (the interface task) and M1-T03 failed to generate. No M1 task builds `run_streams`, `make_schedule`, the colearn schedules or `test_lineup`, even though PL-01's `train_loop` needs them. Plan and tests still use the old fields `points`/`points_after` and the old folder layout `<learner>/<reward>`. So the first ready task can't be built. Set B departs more from the ground truth. It has no random baseline. It allows a $5 rented-compute budget when the project has none beyond free tools. It never teaches reward shaping. Its own risk section admits the tank as specified lets a fish see the ball only one step before contact, so 'no fish can dodge what it sees'. Its build layer, though, is coherent: M1 is a real walking skeleton, one interface task freezes all seven M1 packages with fakes and samples, the packets are complete, the dependency graph uses fakes so spines run in parallel, and roadmap, plan and todo agree. Weighing a mostly unbuildable but sound plan against a buildable plan with design gaps, B scores higher overall.

strengths: Thorough, sound RL spec: random and scripted baselines everywhere, a before/after comparison for each added piece, reward shaping, PG ladder, co-learning ladder with controls, version tournament
Careful reproducibility and seed-stream design (AD-05) and per-environment reports (AD-14)
The core speaks sides and schedules, so all three environments share one loop
weaknesses: M1 plan is stale against the contract; the interface task's packet failed to generate
PL-01 steps run_streams, make_schedule, colearn schedules and test_lineup have no M1 task
Process narration and superseded framing left in architecture.md and pipelines.md
28-row PL-01 step table reads as a registry list rather than a call path

strengths: Real walking-skeleton M1 (train → eval → list) with one interface task freezing every package boundary
Complete, self-contained packets with frozen types and fakes
Dependency graph uses fakes, so spines start in parallel; roadmap, plan and todo agree
Plain first-person brief and spec a solo learner can read
weaknesses: No random baseline, so half the success criterion is missing
Rented GPU budget contradicts the free-tools constraint
Known tank design flaw kept: fish can't dodge a ball they see only one step before contact
Twelve packages, each with four docs, plus explained files, is heavy for a solo learning lab
No reward-shaping concept; library-twin milestones add scope
